quest.title: Rest Beyond Reach
quest.description: Rerir used the cannon in Nasha Town to obtain a complete body. The chaos caused by the Wild Hunt is far from over...
quest.rewards_formatted: Adventure EXP x875, Primogem x30, Mora x38100, Hero's Wit x4, Mystic Enhancement Ore x7

chapter.num: Song of the Welkin Moon: Act II
chapter.title: Elegy of Dust and Lamplight

talks.objective: Return to Nasha Town and reunite with your companions

dialogues.speaker: Black Screen
dialogues.text: Everyone convenes, recounting what happened to them and sharing what they've learned...

dialogues.speaker: Lauma
dialogues.text: Fortunately, we were able to minimize the harm. Only a few townspeople were hurt.

dialogues.speaker: Lauma
dialogues.text: But the Rächer of Solnari has now gained a complete form, while we still know nothing about his goals.

dialogues.speaker: Ineffa
dialogues.text: It seems we have done something akin to releasing a vicious Qucusaur into the wild.

dialogues.speaker: Ineffa
dialogues.text: ...I am sorry. Is no one here familiar with Qucusaurs?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: P—Paimon knows what you mean, but that analogy seems more than slightly understated...

dialogues.speaker: Nefer
dialogues.text: He said that this world means nothing to him, so it is possible that he doesn't have a reason to fight us at the moment.

dialogues.speaker: Nefer
dialogues.text: If his objective had been revenge alone, we would likely have no recourse.

dialogues.speaker: Jahoda
dialogues.text: Is there, uh, still time for me to tender my resignation?

dialogues.speaker: Jahoda
dialogues.text: Just kidding, just kidding! Don't worry, Boss, I know there's no running now!

dialogues.speaker: Aino
dialogues.text: So my cannon, my pride and joy, was a hindrance rather than a help... Gah! You know what? I'm gonna dismantle it, right now!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: That's right, and it still works on normal Wild Hunt anomalies. Don't let this get you down, Aino!

response.speaker: Nefer
response.text: Flins, we'll need you to attend to the aftermath with the Lightkeepers. Don't worry, I've explained everything to them. You're in the clear.

response.speaker: Flins
response.text: My thanks — for that, and for everything else I hear you did to help us arrive at the truth.

response.speaker: Nefer
response.text: Had you been willing to show yourself in public more often, you would not have been so easy to isolate, you know.

response.speaker: Flins
response.text: Heh, point taken. I will give that some thought.

response.speaker: Flins
response.text: Hmm. I suppose that's one way I'd benefit from replacing Sergeant Major Sousi...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: You mean, you're being promoted?

response.speaker: Player
response.text: He's joking, Paimon...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Was Paimon the only one who didn't get that?

response.speaker: Flins
response.text: #Well, {NICKNAME}, if you've got a moment, would you like to come with me?

response.speaker: Flins
response.text: There's a certain gentleman I'd like to send off on his final journey.

dialogues.speaker: Flins
dialogues.text: This man was like a lighthouse...

dialogues.speaker: Flins
dialogues.text: Here he lived, as if it were a mere matter of course, and brought light and grace to those around him. But people, once used to illumination, are apt to ignore the lantern's presence.

dialogues.speaker: Flins
dialogues.text: Slowly, gradually, he came to think as such himself.

dialogues.speaker: Flins
dialogues.text: "I have achieved too little, I must do better, there is more work to be done..."

dialogues.speaker: Flins
dialogues.text: Perhaps his end was tragic, but I remain proud of the way in which he illuminated the path for others.

dialogues.speaker: Flins
dialogues.text: Every shadow born of the light shall remember it.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Poor guy...

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: I once heard the tale of a Lantern Fae.

dialogues.speaker: Flins
dialogues.text: Heh. I've heard that one, too.

choices.text: And I'd like to say the same to him.

response.speaker: Flins
response.text: Is that so?

response.speaker: Flins
response.text: Well, you're right. It may seem that our efforts were in vain, that Rerir achieved his goals.

response.speaker: Flins
response.text: But we will pursue him to the last, even if the outcome is not what we wish for.

response.speaker: Flins
response.text: It is not dissimilar to the role of a Graveyard Keeper...

response.speaker: Flins
response.text: We do not seek to bring the dead back to life, only to grant them peace.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: I'm glad to hear that's how you see it.

response.speaker: Flins
response.text: Yeah.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Wh—What are you two talking about? Care to explain?

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Not right now, Paimon. I'll tell you when we get back.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Okay...

response.speaker: Flins
response.text: Either way, the Lantern Fae is not playing the leading role in these final rites.

response.speaker: Flins
response.text: "Light-bearer, with your blood, you have paved the road to glory and justice."

response.speaker: Flins
response.text: "Even as we hurry on, bruised and battered though we may be, stay awhile and look back upon the world and all its love and hatred."

response.speaker: Flins
response.text: "Until it closes its eyes in the depths of night, and a lantern lit for you alone flickers softly into life."

response.speaker: Flins
response.text: Thank you for everything, Sergeant Major Sousi.

choices.text: There's no need to be so fixated on the outcome.

dialogues.speaker: Aino
dialogues.text: Flins? Don't see you coming around here often. Just feel free to take a look. I'm busy right now.

dialogues.speaker: Flins
dialogues.text: Well, I've come to visit you, Miss Aino. Here — I've brought some snacks from town in their traditional butter flavor. So, where should I leave them...

dialogues.speaker: Aino
dialogues.text: Shh! ... Ineffa might hear you.

dialogues.speaker: Aino
dialogues.text: ...So, what's the occasion? Are you... gonna to say that the Ratniki will be taking over all Wild Hunt incidents after that hiccup with the cannon?

dialogues.speaker: Flins
dialogues.text: And criticize a genius like yourself on account of results that none of us could anticipate? We would not be that crass.

dialogues.speaker: Flins
dialogues.text: If we really did do that, I daresay we shall never again see technological breakthroughs.

dialogues.speaker: Aino
dialogues.text: Hmph. Sweet-talker...

dialogues.speaker: Flins
dialogues.text: It gladdens me to have set your heart at ease.

dialogues.speaker: Aino
dialogues.text: Anyway, what's the matter, exactly?

dialogues.speaker: Flins
dialogues.text: Well. Could you help me repair this lantern? I did bring it to Nasha Town to get it fixed, but it broke again during our previous battle.

dialogues.speaker: Aino
dialogues.text: You want a genius like me to go fix a lantern?

dialogues.speaker: Flins
dialogues.text: Oh, my apologies. Perhaps this request should be better directed to Miss Ineffa, and perhaps the snacks too...

dialogues.speaker: Aino
dialogues.text: Wh—Wh—Wh... I... I mean, I can totally do this, no problem. Wait right there. I'll be done before you can say "Fix-it!"

dialogues.speaker: Flins
dialogues.text: Much obliged, then.

dialogues.speaker: Aino
dialogues.text: And next time this happens to you, make sure to come to me first, you hear?

dialogues.speaker: Ineffa
dialogues.text: Krumkake creation complete. Please, enjoy while it's hot.

dialogues.speaker: Lauma
dialogues.text: Thank you for going to the trouble of remembering that, Miss Ineffa. May this taste bear witness to a friendship that will endure forever and a day.

dialogues.speaker: Ineffa
dialogues.text: Understood. However, I fear that krumkakes do not keep for that long. A week at most may pass before their taste deteriorates.

dialogues.speaker: Lauma
dialogues.text: Hehe, that's not quite what I meant by... Hmm?

dialogues.speaker: Ineffa
dialogues.text: Oh? We appear to have some guests.

dialogues.speaker: Lauma
dialogues.text: Ah, they must have followed the aroma of the krumkake... It's alright, come closer. Ineffa is a friend.

dialogues.speaker: Ineffa
dialogues.text: Affirmative. In fact, I can devise a cereal omelette based on individual preferences, before crushing it into servings to share around.

dialogues.speaker: Ineffa
dialogues.text: What are they saying?

dialogues.speaker: Lauma
dialogues.text: They... are discussing your address. They wish to go home with you.

dialogues.speaker: Jahoda
dialogues.text: Boss, I... Do you remember that thing... that I wanted to ask your opinion about?

dialogues.speaker: Jahoda
dialogues.text: On a scale of 1 to 10, how much effort should the Curatorium of Secrets put in if we were to work with others again?

dialogues.speaker: Nefer
dialogues.text: Hehe.

dialogues.speaker: Jahoda
dialogues.text: Is that a 1? Isn't that kinda low...

dialogues.speaker: Nefer
dialogues.text: Guess again.

dialogues.speaker: Jahoda
dialogues.text: Wait, you mean zero? But wouldn't we just be slapping our brand on the joint venture and calling it a day? Why even team up at that point?

dialogues.speaker: Nefer
dialogues.text: *sigh* ...Jahoda.

dialogues.speaker: Nefer
dialogues.text: What I mean to say is that there is neither an upper nor lower limit.

dialogues.speaker: Jahoda
dialogues.text: Huh! That's just like you, Boss, always thinking ahead...

dialogues.speaker: Jahoda
dialogues.text: Wait a minute, that's not an answer at all, is it? C'mon, just give me a number, boss, please!

dialogues.speaker: Dori
dialogues.text: Hmm? What brings you here? Didn't expect to see you around again...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: And where have you been, huh? Didn't run away or anything, did ya?

dialogues.speaker: Dori
dialogues.text: Oh, of course not! I was simply elsewhere discussing business deals.

dialogues.speaker: Dori
dialogues.text: Indeed, it was all thanks to you that my little store was saved. *sob* I am grateful. So grateful...

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Okay, okay, you can cut it with the acting now...

dialogues.speaker: Dori
dialogues.text: What? Why, I wasn't acting in the slightest!

dialogues.speaker: Dori
dialogues.text: And didn't I tell you that my prices were reasonable? Ah, but you still turned to that Curatorium of Secrets, or whatever it is they call it.

dialogues.speaker: Dori
dialogues.text: *sigh* If even regulars such as you abandon ship like this, what can a businesswoman do but take her wares elsewhere...?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: You're way too wary of the Curatorium...

dialogues.speaker: Dori
dialogues.text: And how should I not be, hmm? Running small overseas enterprises is no mean feat — never mind when such formidable competition exists...

dialogues.speaker: Dori
dialogues.text: Ah, forget it. Fortune and destiny are as one, so there is no use complaining.

dialogues.speaker: Dori
dialogues.text: It's not as if Nefer did me no favors on account of our common homeland when I first arrived.

dialogues.speaker: Dori
dialogues.text: If anything is to blame, it is the lack of opportunity to have her owe me in turn, big time!

dialogues.speaker: Dori
dialogues.text: Now then! Should she ever need anything, you make sure — no, make doubly sure — to inform me first, alright?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Columbina! What are you doing here?

dialogues.speaker: The Damselette
dialogues.text: Hmm? Was it not you who recommended such walkabouts to me?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Yeah, but aren't you afraid the Fatui will see you?

dialogues.speaker: The Damselette
dialogues.text: Sandrone seems uninterested in my capture, and the others are unlikely to risk making contact at all. They have more troublesome affairs to deal with.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: (Rerir, if I had to guess... He is a threat to all who live in Nod-Krai.)

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Well, it's good to come out for a walk either way. So, how do you feel? Is Nasha Town to your liking?

dialogues.speaker: The Damselette
dialogues.text: Mmm... The flow of kuuvahki is somewhat turbulent, and the people are ill at ease.

dialogues.speaker: The Damselette
dialogues.text: However...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: However?

dialogues.speaker: The Damselette
dialogues.text: Is this where you purchased the dishes you "treated" me to?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: (Are you serious? That's what she's concerned about? Berries and Fried Meat?)

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Um, well, we can take you to grab a bite if you'd like to. There's all sorts of delicious stuff out here that you won't get to try at home.

dialogues.speaker: The Damselette
dialogues.text: ...You've been quite subdued. Thorny questions on your mind, perhaps?

response.speaker: The Damselette
response.text: I could not gain any insight into his schemes, I fear.

response.speaker: The Damselette
response.text: Now that he has donned a shape and form, selling his power short would prove a fatal error.

response.speaker: The Damselette
response.text: But that power of his plays host to an obsession that borders on mania.

response.speaker: The Damselette
response.text: I cannot say if that fixation is directed at the moons or at something else...

response.speaker: The Damselette
response.text: Perhaps understanding the subject of his fixation shall prove key to repelling him in the future...

response.speaker: The Damselette
response.text: Well, Sandrone's daily routine is highly irregular, while The Doctor often orders people around. As for Arlecchino...

response.speaker: The Damselette
response.text: Hmm? Was that not what you were curious about?

response.speaker: The Damselette
response.text: Well then. Have you been to that Experimental Design Bureau of theirs? That "weapon" will play a key role in the Tsaritsa's plan. That's what I've heard, anyway.

response.speaker: The Damselette
response.text: And what plan is that, precisely? Well, I cannot say I care.

choices.text: I've been thinking about our spaceship...

response.speaker: The Damselette
response.text: I could look into the Eternal Moon's marrow for you, if you wish it so.

response.speaker: The Damselette
response.text: But after our previous attempt, I suspect your spaceship has been intentionally hidden away.

response.speaker: The Damselette
response.text: Perhaps someone has certain truths they wish to hide from you, or from others.

response.speaker: The Damselette
response.text: And I doubt there are many who could accomplish such a feat.

response.speaker: The Damselette
response.text: I... still wish to return to the moon that belongs to me.

response.speaker: The Damselette
response.text: That is where the answers lie buried. That... is my true "home."

choices.text: I've been thinking about our spaceship...
I've been thinking about our spaceship...

dialogues.speaker: "Rächer of Solnari"
dialogues.text: ...Interesting.

dialogues.speaker: "Rächer of Solnari"
dialogues.text: You've followed me this far. Why not show your face?
Haha, right, right! Right you are. I forgot to introduce myself.

dialogues.speaker: Varka
dialogues.text: The name's Varka. Knight of Boreas, and Grand Master of the Knights of Favonius.

dialogues.speaker: Aino
dialogues.text: "Fix my lantern," he says. Puh-lease! This won't take ten minutes!

dialogues.speaker: Aino
dialogues.text: If only everyone knew what the heck they were doing...

dialogues.speaker: Aino
dialogues.text: Take that Hintsa for instance. How in the world do you end up creating an integrated controller for the cannon AND the barrier from random components people ask you to fix!? Ugh, gives me a headache just thinking about it...

dialogues.speaker: Aino
dialogues.text: I gave him a real earful, and told him to send me regular reports — if he's been working on it lately, I wanna hear about it! *sigh* Y—Yeah, I mean, I know I'm partly at fault too, alright?

dialogues.speaker: Flins
dialogues.text: #Ah, fancy meeting you here, {NICKNAME}. I've decided my lantern has earned itself some thorough maintenance after that rather intense battle.

dialogues.speaker: Flins
dialogues.text: Thank you for keeping my secrets, despite knowing as much as you do.

choices.text: I didn't have time to ask this before, but...

response.speaker: Flins
response.text: Well, because otherwise, I'd get in trouble with the Starshyna. If they couldn't detect my own lantern, I suspect the higher-ups would foist a standard-issue Ratnik lantern on me.

response.speaker: Flins
response.text: A Ratnik carrying two lanterns — imagine that! It would be an aesthetic transgression of the highest order. Hehe.

choices.text: Why were the Lightkeepers able to detect your lantern?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Hey, it's Luonnotar... Should we go after her? Or do you have someone else you'd like to meet?
